title: 'changes detected' Stop hook prints the real staged diff
userDescription: make the 'changes detected' hook print out what changes are actually staged, because the agent's view of staged changes is always stale.  It should use the same code that the commit-message hook uses to provide the list of staged changes.
goal: - After a turn that edits and stages a file, the Stop hook's additionalContext contains the actual `git diff --staged` text for that file, not only the generic 'Files were changed' sentence.
- The staged-diff text comes from the same scripts/stagedDiffs.ts code path the commit-message skill uses; no second copy of the diff logic exists in the repo.
- The full diff is emitted, not a file-name-only list.
- Staged changes in a submodule whose pointer moved appear in the hook output, labelled per repo, the same way the commit-message skill labels them.
- `npm test` passes, including an updated tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts that asserts the staged-diff text is present in additionalContext.
notInScope: - NOT in scope: changing the commit-message skill's own output or wording, changing the EXCLUDES list in stagedDiffs.ts, and changing the staging behaviour itself -- the hook still only reports, it never stages.
description:
The 'changes detected' hook is scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts (Stop/SubagentStop), which currently only checks `git status --porcelain` column two per file to decide if anything is unstaged, then emits a generic additionalContext string 'Files were changed. Stage the changes...' with no diff content. The commit-message skill already has the reusable staged-diff code in scripts/stagedDiffs.ts: it resolves the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from `process.cwd()`, runs `git diff --staged` with an EXCLUDES filter, and recurses into any submodule whose pointer moved. Note stagedDiffs.ts is currently a top-level script that writes to stdout, not an exported function -- confirm its actual shape in the source before assuming an export exists; extracting a reusable function is expected. stage-and-summarize-stop.ts must call that shared code and include the actual staged-diff text in the additionalContext payload instead of the generic reminder, so the agent sees what is really staged rather than trusting its stale in-context view. The user chose the FULL staged diff, not a file-name-only list, and chose reuse of the same code over a new lighter implementation. Complication: stage-and-summarize-stop.ts iterates over `paths` that can span multiple repos/submodules (using `dirname(p)` per path), while stagedDiffs.ts resolves only one repo root from cwd with no repo parameter, so this task must either loop the stagedDiffs logic per distinct repo root among the flagged paths, or add a repo-path parameter. tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts's `run()` helper currently asserts additionalContext matches /commit-message skill/ and does not exercise diff content, so the tests need updating to assert the emitted diff text appears in additionalContext.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

scripts/stagedDiffs.ts already exports stagedDiffs() (line 27) with a CLI guard at line 55 — the extraction this description asks to confirm is done. It takes no repo argument and resolves a single root from cwd; the remaining work is the repo-path parameter. 'The hook still only reports, it never stages' means not in scope for this task; task 160 owns staging behavior.
tests: Unit test on the hook: create a temp git repo, write and `git add` a file, feed scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts its Stop-hook JSON on stdin (with a turn-flag file listing that path), and assert the printed hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext contains the staged diff text for that file.
problemSolvedByTask: The agent doesn't accurately see what is really staged after the end-of-turn stage-and-summarize-stop.ts hook fires.

title: Add a /mermaid skill that diagrams a codebase into a .mmd file
userDescription: make a '/mermaid' skill that searches a codebase and builds a .mmd mermaid diagram.  it should follow the same mermaid diagram rules that I used for the diagrams in taskTools-86 (Yes/No boxes at decision points, output boxes -> what gets outputted, etc)
goal: - A /mermaid skill exists at skills/mermaid/SKILL.md and appears in the skill list.
- Running /mermaid against a codebase writes a .mmd file the user can name and open.

- The written .mmd follows the diagrams/tackle-tasks grammar: flowchart TB, boxes declared inside subgraphs as BOX_ID["label"], edges written as A -- "label" --> B, decision boxes branch with two edges labeled YES and NO (never separate _YES/_NO boxes), a classDef/class block assigns every box a role, and cross-section targets are grouped in a "next diagram" subgraph joined by an invisible ~~~ link.
- The skill contains an explicit written checklist of those diagram rules, and the skill follows that checklist when it draws.
notInScope: - NOT in scope: changing any existing diagram in diagrams/tackle-tasks/, and changing scripts/generateSteps.ts. The skill only reads generateSteps.ts as the reference parser whose grammar its output must match; the skill's own output documents an arbitrary codebase and need not itself be runnable by generateSteps.ts.
description:
Add a new /mermaid skill (skills/mermaid/SKILL.md, following the existing skill format seen in skills/view-task/SKILL.md and skills/create-task/SKILL.md) that searches a target codebase and emits a .mmd mermaid flowchart. It must codify the diagramming grammar already used in diagrams/tackle-tasks/*.mmd and parsed by scripts/generateSteps.ts (see getEdgesInDiagram and getPromptBoxesInDiagram, roughly lines 60-120, and the `returns_a_prompt` class-role check at line 111 (`getPromptBoxesInDiagram`)): `flowchart TB`, boxes declared inside a named `subgraph ... end` block as `BOX_ID["label"]` (a decision box is a plain rectangular box whose id ends in `_Q`, not a diamond node), edges written `A -- "label" --> B` or `A --> B`, decision boxes branching with two edges whose labels are literally `YES` and `NO` (extra detail can follow on a `
` line) rather than separate `_YES`/`_NO` boxes, a `classDef`/`class` block at the end assigning every box exactly one role among `script`, `returns_a_prompt`, `next_diagram`, `output`, and `fail`, and any box the diagram references but does not itself resolve grouped into a second `subgraph ... ["next diagram"]` block joined to the main subgraph by an invisible `~~~` link. Reference examples: diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-planTheTask.mmd, diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-whatIsReviewVerdict.mmd, and diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-preambleStatusCheck.mmd. No existing skill in skills/ produces diagrams; this is a new skill directory, not an edit to an existing one. The skill must also carry an explicit written checklist of these diagram rules that it follows while it draws. The /mermaid skill documents codebases generally, not just taskTools pipelines, so its output does not need to be runnable by generateSteps.ts (which is hardcoded to the tackle-tasks box-ownership map) — it only needs to follow the same grammar.
tests: skip -- generateSteps.ts is hardcoded to the tackle-tasks pipeline's box-ownership map (BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER) and its cross-diagram remapping, so it cannot run as a general-purpose grammar validator against a diagram of an arbitrary codebase. Acceptance is checked against the written checklist inside the skill itself (every box declared in a subgraph, every edge label cosmetic, every box assigned a class, decision boxes branch on YES/NO edge labels) rather than a runnable script.
problemSolvedByTask: Understanding an unfamiliar codebase's control flow means reading files by hand — no automated way to get a flowchart.

title: Run the full suite on the fresh worktree in the preamble and exit staging-suite-red when staging is red
userDescription:
Run the full suite on the fresh task worktree in the preamble, and stop the run when staging itself is red.

Order of operations for /tackle-tasks N:
1. The existing preamble blocks run as today: PREAMBLE_STATUS_CHECK, IS_TASK_BLOCKED_Q, IS_TASK_ACTIVE_Q, PREFLIGHT_OK_Q, MARK_TASK_ACTIVE.
2. The existing staging code moves staging to the source branch tip: ensureStagingWorktree in scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/stagingWorktree.ts; CREATE_WORKTREE cuts the task worktree from staging; REBASE_RESUMED_WORKTREE_ONTO_STAGING catches a resumed worktree up. Reuse that code; add no new git operations for staging.
3. NEW: right after the worktree exists and holds the lease and submodules (after INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY, before DOCUMENT_GENERATION), a new mutating block RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE runs the full suite inside the task worktree, using the same code RUN_FULL_SUITE uses (scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/runFullSuite.ts, with the knownFailingTests.json baseline from the project root).
4. NEW: a decision block DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q. YES: continue to DOCUMENT_GENERATION and the rest of the pipeline. NO: exit through REPORT_ONLY_EXIT with a new exit type `staging-suite-red` and an exit note that says the suite fails on staging before the task changed anything, lists the new failing tests, and says the suite needs fixing first before the task can run. The worktree is preserved. The task is marked inactive and the lease released, the same way the other report-only exits do it.
5. On a resumed worktree that already carries task commits, the suite is not run by these new blocks; that case keeps today's path.

Why: task 36 ran to suite-red after IMPLEMENT_TASK because a test that was already red on staging (tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts) is outside the task's owned files, so FIX_THE_CODEBASE_FOR_SUITE correctly refused to touch it. The run spent two plan rounds, two reviews, an implementation, and two fix attempts before finding out. The check belongs at the start.

Files: diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-preambleStatusCheck.mmd; new scripts/tackle-tasks/preambleStatusCheck/RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE.ts, RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE.template.json, RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE.test.ts, DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q.ts, DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q.template.json, DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q.test.ts; scripts/tackle-tasks/diagram-steps.json (regenerated by generateSteps, mutating flag set on the new run block); scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/runFullSuite.ts only if it needs a parameter to run before any task commit exists; tests/tackleTasksAcceptance.test.ts (drivers must expect the new blocks in `ran`); scripts/tackle-tasks/reportOnlyExit/*.ts if the exit type needs registering there.

Goal:
- node --test on the two new test files passes
- tests/tackleTasksAcceptance.test.ts passes with the new blocks in every driver's expected `ran`
- A fixture whose staging has a red test outside the task's files exits `staging-suite-red` before DOCUMENT_GENERATION, with the worktree preserved and the task inactive
- A fixture whose staging is green reaches DOCUMENT_GENERATION as today

Not in scope: changing which files FIX_THE_CODEBASE_FOR_SUITE may edit; moving knownFailingTests.json; changing how staging is moved.
goal: - A worktree for task N spawned from staging (where staging is aligned with HEAD and HEAD's test suite fails to pass) is created but the workflow exits before document generation occurs and reports that the test suite is failing.

- A worktree for task N spawned from staging (where staging is aligned with HEAD and HEAD's test suite is passing) is created and the workflow makes it past the 'run the full suite before generating docs' step.
- No new code related to moving staging to HEAD is created.
notInScope: - Changing which files FIX_THE_CODEBASE_FOR_SUITE may edit; that block keeps its owned-files fence.
- Moving knownFailingTests.json or changing where the baseline is read from.
- Changing how staging is moved; ensureStagingWorktree, CREATE_WORKTREE, and REBASE_RESUMED_WORKTREE_ONTO_STAGING stay as they are.
problemSolvedByTask: a failing test suite that existing on the branch that 'staging' and the worktree were cut from prevents the workflow from getting past the 'run the test suite' block, blocking the entire run from completing, because the workflow agents can't touch the files causing the failing tests, because those files are not in the task's modifiableFiles list.
description:
Insert two new blocks into the preamble diagram between INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY and DOCUMENT_GENERATION: RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE (mutating, calls scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/runFullSuite.ts, modeled on scripts/tackle-tasks/runFullSuite/RUN_FULL_SUITE.ts's structure) and DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q (decision: YES continues to DOCUMENT_GENERATION, NO sets a new `staging-suite-red` exitType/exitNote and routes to pipeline-reportOnlyExit.mmd::REPORT_ONLY_EXIT, same pattern as IS_TASK_BLOCKED_Q.ts's "blocked" exit). Only run RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE on the CREATE_WORKTREE/RESET_WORKTREE path (fresh or reset worktree with no task commits yet), not on the REBASE_RESUMED_WORKTREE_ONTO_STAGING path (resumed worktree with existing task commits) — the diagram's DOES_FENCE_COVER_WORKTREE_Q branch continues straight to INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY/DOCUMENT_GENERATION as today. `staging-suite-red` must be added to the TaskExitType union in scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/taskRunState.ts and the EXIT_TYPES array in scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/writeTaskExitNotes.ts, mirroring how `blocked`/`invalid-number`/existing `suite-red` are registered. RUN_FULL_SUITE's existing pattern (scripts/tackle-tasks/runFullSuite/RUN_FULL_SUITE.ts) always targets "staging" as the base branch and reads the baseline via runFullSuite's own readKnownFailingTests(projectRoot) call (scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/taskTestsRunner.ts) — the new block reuses this without needing prepared-task fencing data (ownedFilePaths/testFilePaths), since no task changes exist yet. diagram-steps.json is generated output (see scripts/tackle-tasks/generateSteps or similar) and must be regenerated, not hand-edited, with the new block(s) marked mutating. tests/tackleTasksAcceptance.test.ts drives the preamble via runHookOnce and asserts each fixture's `ran` array of visited box names — every driver whose fixture worktree is freshly created (not a resumed-with-commits case) needs the two new box names inserted between INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY and DOCUMENT_GENERATION.

## Clarification answer (2026-09-07)

Do not edit `scripts/tackle-tasks/preambleStatusCheck/INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY.ts` or its template. Use a new decision block instead.

The packet already carries `docsMode` when it reaches INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY (field declared in `scripts/tackle-tasks/preambleStatusCheck/_packet.ts`). `TAKE_WORKTREE_LEASE.ts` and `RESET_WORKTREE.ts` set it to `AUTOGEN` (fresh or reset worktree). `DOES_FENCE_COVER_WORKTREE_Q.ts` sets it to `UPDATE` (resumed worktree with task commits). That value is the fresh-vs-resumed signal.

Routing:
- In `diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-preambleStatusCheck.mmd`, change the edge `INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY --> DOCUMENT_GENERATION` to `INIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSIVELY --> IS_WORKTREE_FRESH_Q`.
- New decision block `IS_WORKTREE_FRESH_Q` (shape of `DOES_WORKTREE_EXIST_Q.ts`: strip `next`, return `{...packet, box, scriptSignal: CONTINUE, next}`). `docsMode === "AUTOGEN"` -> `next: "RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE"`. `docsMode === "UPDATE"` -> `next: "DOCUMENT_GENERATION"`. Any other value: throw, the same way `DOCUMENT_GENERATION.ts` throws on an unknown docs mode.
- `RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE --> DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q`; YES -> `DOCUMENT_GENERATION`, NO -> report-only exit `staging-suite-red`, as the task already says.

The three IS_WORKTREE_FRESH_Q files are added to this task's owned files.

## Clarification answer (2026-09-07)

Do not add `scripts/tackle-tasks/generateSteps.ts`. It must not change.

The mutating flag is hand-written by design. `scripts/tackle-tasks/generateSteps.ts` line 182 says: "The mutating flag is hand-written, so regenerating from the arrows must not drop it." `getMutatingFromPreviousConfig` reads the flag from the existing `scripts/tackle-tasks/diagram-steps.json` and carries it forward; the generator never derives it from a template or script. Every existing mutating block (CREATE_WORKTREE, RESET_WORKTREE, RUN_FULL_SUITE, and the rest) got its flag that way.

Procedure for the new block:
1. Run the generator so `scripts/tackle-tasks/diagram-steps.json` gains the new entries.
2. Add `"mutating": true` to the `RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE` entry in `scripts/tackle-tasks/diagram-steps.json` by hand. The task owns that file. This is the one field in that file that is meant to be hand-edited.
3. Run the generator again and confirm the flag survives. That confirms step 2 is correct.

`IS_WORKTREE_FRESH_Q` and `DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q` are decisions and get no flag.

## Clarification answer (2026-09-07)

Correction to the earlier answer: `scripts/tackle-tasks/generateSteps.ts` IS in this task's owned files, for one edit only.

That file keeps a hand-written owner map, `BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER` (line 11). Its `assertNoOrphanBoxScripts` guard throws when a box script exists in a folder but the box is not listed under that folder. Commit af19d91 added its new preamble boxes the same way.

The only permitted edit to that file: add `"IS_WORKTREE_FRESH_Q"`, `"RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE"`, and `"DOES_FRESH_WORKTREE_SUITE_PASS_Q"` to the `preambleStatusCheck` array of `BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER`. Change nothing else in it.

Then run the generator (`node scripts/tackle-tasks/generateSteps.ts`) so `scripts/tackle-tasks/diagram-steps.json` is generated, not hand-written. After it runs, add `"mutating": true` to the `RUN_SUITE_ON_FRESH_WORKTREE` entry by hand, and run the generator once more to confirm the flag survives.

The task worktree already holds the nine new block files, the diagram edit, the exit-type registration, and the acceptance tests, all uncommitted. Keep that work. Do not start over.
